name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.192.0 — The build driver's already-DONE refusal now covers both admission branches instead of only the implementing resume. A spec whose closed document was reverted to hardened — the shape a stale blob committed from another session produces — used to walk straight past the ledger check, and the hardened branch's own writes flipped status and stamped diff_base at a HEAD that already contained the shipped work, so red-check's pre-image and the dirty-path check were satisfied by construction and the rebuild proceeded blind. The refusal now runs before any write on either path, and names the reverted status, the git log -S command that finds the close commit, and superseded as the only route to a deliberate rebuild. 7.191.0 — The AskUserQuestion style gate's model judge no longer blocks: it allows the question and returns its verdict to the session as advice. The judge is non-deterministic — one identical question measured one rewrite, six passes, and one silent no-output in eight runs — so a blocking verdict trapped sessions in a loop no rewrite could clear, and the escape (deciding in prose outside the tool) is a dismissed question that stops the run. A false derive verdict was worse still, instructing the session to invent an answer the user never gave. The deterministic tier-1 floor still blocks. Merge strategy is now derived from the driver's own recommendation instead of asked, per the two-lens filter: it has no product consequence and its delivery consequence is already in the printed history. 7.190.0 — The retired HTML design atlas — the whole-product design script, the components duplicate checker, eighteen browser and notes libraries under scripts/lib, the chrome mocks, and the design templates behind them — is deleted outright, along with the command that served it and the spec-paths keys that named it; genesis's no-mock-app skeleton branch drops the HTML checks that used to spawn them (the components duplicate check, the shell check, the shell-stamp check, and the mocks matrix check), so a host with no mock app lands the skeleton with no HTML-design checks; docs/canonical/scripts.md and genesis.md are reworded to name the survivor alone.
